extracted.intended_audience: general public interested in comedy, culture, and politics
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and insights related to creating and performing politically provocative comedy (especially about high-profile figures), including craft choices, historical context, audience impact, and career/distribution risks. Drawn from an interview-style news transcript about Kathy Griffin.

rubrics_metrics.name: Comedian's civic role: political critique as stabilizer
rubrics_metrics.description: "The ability to just do the job, to show up and say the president is bad, is very important as a stabilizing factor of our society, to be reminded that we are allowed to do that." (Jesse David Fox)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Treat political comedy as serving a civic function: part of its value is openly criticizing powerful figures. When evaluating or producing political jokes, consider their role in public discourse beyond pure entertainment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Audibility and access: jokes must be heard to be funny
rubrics_metrics.description: "It's only funny if you can hear the jokes." (Sam Sanders / NPR)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure performance conditions and distribution let the audience actually hear and understand the material. Technical clarity, venue choice, and securing a distributor/platform are part of whether a joke succeeds.

rubrics_metrics.name: Know your comedy history before judgment
rubrics_metrics.description: "Learn your comedy history." (Kathy Griffin responding to 'stay in your lane' critiques)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Contextualize provocative choices within comedy tradition. When producing or critiquing material, be aware of historical precedents and how similar moves have functioned for past comedians.

rubrics_metrics.name: 'Stay in your lane' vs. artistic freedom
rubrics_metrics.description: Discussion of the admonition to 'stay in your lane, tell your jokes' with Griffin's pushback.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Balance respecting one's strengths ('stay in your lane') with artistic freedom to make statements; don't dismiss boundary-pushing without historical/contextual understanding.

rubrics_metrics.name: Half-statement, half-joke format is a recognized approach
rubrics_metrics.description: "There are many, many comedians... that at some point will do something that is half-statement, half-joke." (Kathy Griffin)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Mixing explicit statement and joke is an established stylistic choice. Evaluate such material on both rhetorical clarity (the statement) and comedic effectiveness (the joke).

rubrics_metrics.name: Weigh career, legal, and personal risks of provocation
rubrics_metrics.description: Griffin recounts losing work, being blacklisted, federal officials threatening charges, and being detained at airports after the image controversy.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When producing provocative political comedy, explicitly consider potential career fallout, legal scrutiny, travel/ security impacts, and personal consequences; these are legitimate evaluation criteria for whether to proceed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provocative imagery can amplify message but invite severe backlash
rubrics_metrics.description: Griffin's use of a photo of herself holding a mock-severed Trump head (ketchup-covered mask) as an act intended to 'shame Trump.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Using shocking visual satire can powerfully communicate intent but also magnify backlash. Evaluate the proportionality of the provocation to the message and plan for reputational and market consequences.

rubrics_metrics.name: Experimentation and frequent testing of material
rubrics_metrics.description: "In between, like, gigs, I will just do a million crazy things to try to make you laugh." (Kathy Griffin)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Encourage iterative testing and experimentation with jokes and formats. Frequent low-stakes trials help develop material and gauge audience reaction before major public release.

rubrics_metrics.name: Distribution and gatekeeping affect comedy's reach
rubrics_metrics.description: Griffin's new comedy special is 'on ice' because she 'can't find a distributor.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess distribution options and market receptivity as part of producing controversial comedy. Even well-crafted material can fail to reach audiences without acceptable distribution channels.
